edits.before: Protect establishment; inspect and hand-pick in damp weather.
edits.after: Protect transplants with greased collars made of cardboard or sectioned plastic bottles.

edits.alt: Healthy plant remains going into a compost bin

edits.before: Mulch generously and leave enough room for the chosen bush or trailing type. Avoid poorly drained ground.
edits.after: A pocket is a hole about 12 in. deep and wide. Refill with soil mixed with mature compost or well-rotted manure, leaving a slight mound. For No-Dig, just make a low mound of compost; don't dig down.

edits.before: Mulch generously and leave enough room for the chosen bush or trailing type. Avoid poorly drained ground.
edits.after: A pocket is a hole about 30 cm deep and wide. Refill with soil mixed with mature compost or well-rotted manure, leaving a slight mound. For No-Dig, just make a low mound of compost; don't dig down.

edits.before: Let insects reach the flowers. If fruit fails to set, transfer pollen from a male flower to the centre of a female flower, recognisable by the tiny fruit behind it.
edits.after: Let insects reach the flowers. If fruit fails to set, transfer pollen from a male to the centre of a female flower (with the tiny fruit behind).

edits.alt: Courgette transplant being planted into a compost-enriched pocket, shown in cutaway.
